title: More __init__
goal: This lesson covers richer __init__ setups with more attributes, and starting values you set yourself.
learn: Set starting values like lives or balance
Create ready to use objects in one line
idea: __init__ can set lots of fields at once, like name, level, lives, and score. You can also give starting values that the caller does not pass in, like self.lives = 3 every time. That is one construction line and a fully ready object.
changeOneLine: In the editor above, change the starting lives to 5 and press Run. The status should show Lives 5.

practice.text: Monster __init__(name, hp). Also set self.power = 5. Create one and print all three.
practice.hint: Store name and hp from the parameters on self, and then set self.power = 5 even though callers do not pass power.
practice.starterTip: self.name = name, self.hp = hp, and self.power = 5. The three prints at the bottom should work.
practice.gradingNote: Pass if power defaults to 5 and name/hp stored.

practice.text: Account(owner, balance) with __init__. Create and print a sentence with both fields.
practice.hint: In __init__, set self.owner and self.balance from the parameters. Then print() should use a.owner and a.balance.
practice.starterTip: self.owner = owner and self.balance = balance, then print(a.owner, "has", a.balance).
practice.gradingNote: Pass if sentence uses owner and balance attributes.

quiz.question: Can __init__ set attributes not passed as parameters?
quiz.correct: Right, something like self.lives = 3 is fine.

quiz.question: After p = Player('Sam', 2), is p.score ready if init set it?
quiz.correct: Yes, init runs while the object is being built.

quiz.question: Why put setup in __init__?
quiz.correct: Right, every new object starts complete.
quiz.wrong: It is a consistent starting state.

project.title: Hero Sheet
project.desc: Make a Hero with __init__(name, strength) that also sets self.hp = 10 and self.gold = 0. Print a three line sheet for one hero.
